graph.title: Reaction game (micro:bit)
notes: This is a MakeCode block-programming project. The only hardware is a micro:bit using its built-in 5x5 LED display and on-board buttons A and B. The manual shows no wires, breadboard or external components.

Assumption: the manual says to write the program in the MakeCode editor and transfer the .hex file onto the micro:bit. That needs a USB cable, and the micro:bit needs power, so I added one USB cable (usb1) joined to the micro:bit's USB port. The manual does not show it, and its far end (computer or power) is left unmodelled.
The micro:bit is not in the catalogue, so I added a new part type 'microbit'. Its ports are the two on-board buttons and the USB connector.
The program logic (forever loop, random pause, while not A and not B pressed, if A/B shows an arrow) is software and is not modelled as graph edges.
The two images show the 'while not (A pressed) and not (B pressed)' block, in Arabic. They agree with the manual's text.
